description: We are a driven, multidisciplinary team passionate about using science, technology, and creative design to solve real-world challenges. Combining strong analytical research, UI/UX prototyping, and strategic problem-solving, we aim to build an innovative, high-impact project from the ground up.
summary:
We developed the Earth System Trend Detective, an interactive, no-code web dashboard designed to transform complex NASA satellite and climate model datasets into clear, actionable visual insights.
NASA’s Earth-observing missions generate massive volumes of multidimensional data, making it difficult for non-specialists to select the right indicators, track multi-decadal shifts across contrasting regions, and distinguish genuine climate trends from natural seasonal fluctuations. Our tool directly addresses this challenge through a streamlined analytical engine built around four core questions: what is changing (tracking variables like surface temperature anomalies, sea ice extent, \text{CO}_2, and vegetation indices from GISTEMP, NSIDC, OCO-2, and MODIS), where it is changing (comparing global baselines against regional hotspots), how much it is changing (computing automated linear regression slopes), and whether the shift is statistically significant (evaluating p-value thresholds).
This project is important because it democratizes Earth science exploration. By eliminating programming barriers and pairing visual storytelling with statistical validation, it empowers students, researchers, and local planners to monitor critical environmental risks—such as extreme heat and desertification—and make informed, data-driven decisions for a sustainable future.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web dashboard that turns complex NASA Earth science data into clear, easy-to-read visualizations. Users choose an environmental variable (surface temperature, Arctic sea ice, atmospheric CO₂, or vegetation health), a time range, and a region, then instantly see how things are changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant or just natural variability.

Benefits and impact: It removes the technical barrier of raw satellite data formats and programming skills, so anyone from students to regional planners can explore real climate trends. It builds climate data literacy in classrooms and gives communities, especially in climate-vulnerable areas like the Middle East, quick insight into heat, water scarcity, and land degradation.

Tools and data: The tool is modeled on NASA datasets (GISTEMP, NSIDC sea ice records, OCO-2, and MODIS) and uses linear regression and significance testing. [Add your coding languages and software here.]

Creativity: It doesn't just show data; it interprets it in plain language and compares global averages with regional hotspots to show how one planetary driver can affect places differently.

Factors considered: Accessibility, scientific credibility, statistical rigor, regional relevance, and scalability. Future versions will add live NASA data feeds, anomaly alerts, and downloadable reports.
